reviewed_by: Claude review of compaction capacity errors
reason: ContextCompactor.compact wrapped every failure from the hierarchical memory pass in a plain ContextCompactionError after persisting the FAILED snapshot, so a ContextCapacityError (a window too small for a faithful summary, or derived context that cannot fit the compactor) lost its subclass. chat.py maps ContextCapacityError to a 422 ChatConfigurationError and the base class to a ChatCompactionError that api.py answers with 503, retryable=True and Retry-After: 1, so a deterministic capacity failure was presented to the operator as a transient outage and each client retry ran the same failing pass and persisted another FAILED snapshot. The except path now re-raises ContextCapacityError as ContextCapacityError with the same safe message and usage, and the base class otherwise. test_context gains a case with a 600-token window that asserts the capacity type reaches the caller, no provider request is made, and the FAILED snapshot is still persisted; the rest of the file covers the provenance-repair and hierarchical paths that share the except block.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change; the 422 versus 503 mapping already exists in chat.py and api.py. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the remaining-core fallback for context.py) is the real-Core journey suite and does not drive compaction to a capacity failure. No full suites.
